provenance.pins: datasheet p.3 Pin Functions table (VSSOP-10). vMax values are from the Absolute Maximum Ratings table, not from the pin table.

notes: Common-mode and VBUS absolute max 40 V. On a 36 V bus that is only 1.11x margin, so it is NOT usable high-side here.

Used LOW SIDE instead - shunt in the ground return, common mode near 0 V, so the 40 V rating is irrelevant. Costs the ability to detect an output short to ground, and lifts the load ground by 25 mV at 5 A through a 5 mOhm shunt.

RANGE IS SET BY THE SHUNT, AND THE FULL-SCALE CURRENT IS NOT THE CONTRACT. The differential input is +-81.92 mV, so a 5 mOhm shunt measures to 16.4 A and a 10 mOhm one only to 8.19 A. Size it against what the return can actually carry - on the LED matrix controller that is the 8.0 A full-white flash and the 11.1 A the two eFuses can pass before either limits, not the 5 A PD contract. Saturation does not stop ALERT firing if its threshold is below full scale, but it does stop the reading being a measurement, and a software power limiter reasons in watts from that reading.
The 85 V parts that would have allowed high-side sensing (INA228, INA238) are both at zero stock at LCSC, which is what forced this. Low-side turned out to be the better answer anyway.

INPUT SERIES RESISTORS. SS7.4.2 p.14 asks for 10 Ohm in series with IN+ and IN- in any application without a large electrolytic on either side of the shunt. That is the common case for a low-side sense on a ceramic-only board, and it was missed here for sixteen review rounds because every other support component the datasheet names was present.

rules.note: datasheet: a 0.1 uF bypass at VS. C20.

open-drain output - it cannot assert high without a pull-up (R45 on the LED matrix controller). Configured as a shunt-overvoltage comparator it is the only sub-millisecond hardware shed path on the board.
